title: 2 Samuel Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 13.

questions.question: Who was the fair sister of Absalom mentioned in 2 Samuel 13?
questions.correctAnswer: Tamar
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:1 states that Absalom had a fair sister named Tamar.

questions.question: Why did Amnon become sick according to 2 Samuel 13?
options: Because he loved Tamar and was vexed
Because he was weak from battle
questions.correctAnswer: Because he loved Tamar and was vexed
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:2 says Amnon was vexed and fell sick for his sister Tamar because he loved her.

questions.question: Who was Amnon's friend who gave him advice?
questions.correctAnswer: Jonadab
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:3 identifies Jonadab, son of Shimeah, as Amnon's friend who was very subtil.

questions.question: What advice did Jonadab give to Amnon to get Tamar to come to him?
options: Ask the king to send her
Make himself sick and ask Tamar to serve him
Send a message requesting her presence
questions.correctAnswer: Make himself sick and ask Tamar to serve him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:5 explains Jonadab told Amnon to feign sickness and request Tamar to bring him food and serve him.

questions.question: How did Amnon respond when Tamar first brought him cakes?
options: He refused to eat and sent everyone out
He gave them back to Tamar
questions.correctAnswer: He refused to eat and sent everyone out
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:9 states Amnon refused to eat the cakes and told all men to leave him.

questions.question: What did Amnon say to Tamar after she brought him food into the chamber?
options: Come lie with me, my sister
Tell the king I am sick
questions.correctAnswer: Come lie with me, my sister
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:11 records Amnon telling Tamar to come lie with him after she brought the cakes into the chamber.

questions.question: How did Tamar respond to Amnon's request to lie with her?
options: She said it was a foolish and improper thing
She told the king right away
questions.correctAnswer: She said it was a foolish and improper thing
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:12 shows Tamar told Amnon not to force her because such a thing is not done in Israel and called it folly.

questions.question: True or False: Amnon listened to Tamar's plea and did not force her.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:14 states Amnon did not listen to Tamar but forced her because he was stronger.

questions.question: What was Amnon's attitude toward Tamar immediately after he forced her?
questions.correctAnswer: He hated her exceedingly
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:15 says Amnon hated her more after forcing her than he had loved her.

questions.question: What garment was Tamar wearing that identified her as a king's virgin daughter?
questions.correctAnswer: A robe of many colors
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:18 explains Tamar wore a garment of divers colours typical for king's daughters that were virgins.

questions.question: What did Tamar do after being sent away by Amnon?
options: She put ashes on her head and rent her garment
She stayed silent and went to her chamber
questions.correctAnswer: She put ashes on her head and rent her garment
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:19 records Tamar putting ashes on her head, tearing her garment, and crying after Amnon sent her away.

questions.question: True or False: Absalom told Tamar to keep quiet about what Amnon had done.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:20 shows Absalom told Tamar to hold her peace about Amnon's assault because he was her brother.

questions.question: What was King David's reaction upon hearing of what Amnon did to Tamar?
questions.correctAnswer: He was very wroth
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:21 states that King David was very angry when he heard what happened.

questions.question: True or False: Jonadab assured King David that all the king's sons were killed by Absalom.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:32-33 indicates Jonadab told David only Amnon was dead, not all the king's sons.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 13, which event comes first?
options: Absalom invites the king's sons to sheepshearers
Amnon makes himself sick to get Tamar to come
Tamar puts ashes on her head
questions.correctAnswer: Amnon makes himself sick to get Tamar to come
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:5-6 shows Amnon pretending to be sick to lure Tamar before other events occur later in the chapter.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: After Amnon forced Tamar, what was his attitude towards her?
options: He loved her more than before
questions.correctAnswer: He hated her exceedingly
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:15 states that Amnon hated Tamar exceedingly, and this hatred was greater than the love he had before. This shows the drastic change in his feelings after the act described in 2 Samuel 13:14.

questions.question: What did Tamar say was worse than the act Amnon committed against her?
questions.correctAnswer: Sending her away
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 13:16, Tamar said the evil in sending her away was greater than the other evil Amnon did to her, emphasizing the depth of her distress and the injustice of being cast out.

questions.question: What did Amnon command his servant to do after forcing Tamar?
options: Send Tamar away and bolt the door
questions.correctAnswer: Send Tamar away and bolt the door
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:17 says Amnon ordered his servant to put Tamar out and bolt the door after her, showing his rejection of her despite his earlier actions described in 2 Samuel 13:14.

questions.question: What was significant about Tamar's garment mentioned in the chapter?
options: It was a garment of divers colours, worn by king's daughters who were virgins
questions.correctAnswer: It was a garment of divers colours, worn by king's daughters who were virgins
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:18 notes Tamar wore a garment of divers colours, which was the apparel for the king's virgin daughters, highlighting her status before the tragic event described in 2 Samuel 13:14.

questions.question: How did Tamar respond after being sent away by Amnon?
options: She put ashes on her head, rent her garment, and wept
She went to the king immediately
questions.correctAnswer: She put ashes on her head, rent her garment, and wept
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:19 describes Tamar's sorrowful response: she put ashes on her head, tore her garment, laid her hand on her head, and cried, showing her grief and mourning after the assault.

questions.question: What advice did Absalom give Tamar after the incident with Amnon?
options: Hold her peace and regard Amnon as her brother
questions.correctAnswer: Hold her peace and regard Amnon as her brother
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 13:20, Absalom tells Tamar to hold her peace and regard Amnon as her brother despite what happened, showing a complex response that reflects family loyalty amid tragedy.

questions.question: How did King David react upon hearing about what Amnon had done to Tamar?
questions.correctAnswer: He was very wroth
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:21 states that King David was very angry when he heard about Amnon's actions, indicating his displeasure though he did not act immediately.

questions.question: Why did Absalom hate Amnon?
options: Because Amnon was the eldest son
Because Amnon was favored by David
Because Amnon refused to fight him
questions.correctAnswer: Because Amnon forced Tamar
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:22 explains that Absalom hated Amnon because he had forced his sister Tamar, highlighting the cause of deep family conflict.

questions.question: What event did Absalom organize two years after the incident with Amnon?
questions.correctAnswer: Sheepshearers in Baalhazor
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:23 records that after two years, Absalom had sheepshearers in Baalhazor and invited all the king's sons, setting the stage for his planned revenge.

questions.question: What was King David's initial response to Absalom's invitation to the sheepshearers?
options: He said no because he did not want to be a burden
questions.correctAnswer: He said no because he did not want to be a burden
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:25 shows David telling Absalom not all should go because they might be chargeable to him, reflecting a cautious and considerate attitude.

questions.question: How did Absalom ensure Amnon would attend the sheepshearers?
options: He pressed the king until he allowed Amnon to go
He sent servants to bring Amnon
He did not want Amnon to attend
questions.correctAnswer: He pressed the king until he allowed Amnon to go
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:27 states that Absalom pressed the king so that Amnon and all the king's sons would go with him, showing determination to include Amnon in his plan.

questions.question: What instructions did Absalom give his servants regarding Amnon at the sheepshearers?
options: To observe Amnon's behavior and kill him when he is merry with wine
To invite Amnon to speak publicly
questions.correctAnswer: To observe Amnon's behavior and kill him when he is merry with wine
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:28 shows Absalom commanding his servants to kill Amnon when he is merry with wine, revealing his plan for revenge due to what Amnon did to Tamar.

questions.question: What was the immediate outcome for Amnon at the sheepshearers?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:29 confirms that Absalom's servants killed Amnon as commanded, fulfilling Absalom's plan described in 2 Samuel 13:28.

questions.question: When David heard the news that Absalom had slain all his sons, he tore his garments and lay on the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 13:30-31 records David's grief expressed by tearing his garments and lying on the ground after hearing the report, showing his deep sorrow.

questions.question: Jonadab assured King David that all of his sons were dead.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 13:32-33, Jonadab tells David not to think all the king's sons were dead, only Amnon was killed, correcting the false report David received in 2 Samuel 13:30.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 13.

questions.question: What was Absalom’s specific instruction to his servants regarding Amnon at the feast?
options: To watch Amnon carefully and kill him when he was merry with wine
To serve Amnon extra food and wine to make him sick
To isolate Amnon from all guests during the feast
To convince Amnon to confess his sins to King David
questions.correctAnswer: To watch Amnon carefully and kill him when he was merry with wine
questions.explanation: Absalom commanded his servants to mark when Amnon's heart was merry with wine and then to smite him, as recorded in 2 Samuel 13:28.

questions.question: What was King David’s initial reaction upon hearing the news that Absalom had slain all the king's sons?
options: He arose, tore his garments, and lay on the earth
He immediately sent soldiers to capture Absalom
He ignored the news and continued his duties
questions.correctAnswer: He arose, tore his garments, and lay on the earth
questions.explanation: The king's grief is shown by him tearing his garments and lying on the earth when he believed all his sons were slain, as described in 2 Samuel 13:31.

questions.question: Who reassured King David that not all his sons had been killed and explained the truth about Amnon’s death?
options: The young man who kept the watch
questions.correctAnswer: Jonadab, the son of Shimeah
questions.explanation: Jonadab, David’s nephew and friend of Amnon, told the king that only Amnon was dead according to Absalom’s plan (2 Samuel 13:32).

questions.question: After the assassination of Amnon, where did Absalom flee to?
options: Geshur, the land of Talmai, son of Ammihud
Jerusalem, to hide in the palace
questions.correctAnswer: Geshur, the land of Talmai, son of Ammihud
questions.explanation: Absalom fled to Geshur and stayed there for three years as stated in 2 Samuel 13:37-38.

questions.question: How long did Absalom stay in Geshur after fleeing?
questions.correctAnswer: Three years
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that Absalom stayed in Geshur for three years (2 Samuel 13:38).

questions.question: What was King David’s emotional state towards Absalom during his exile in Geshur?
options: He mourned for him every day and longed to go to him
He was indifferent and did not care about Absalom
He was angry and sought to punish him further
He forgot about him and focused on other sons
questions.correctAnswer: He mourned for him every day and longed to go to him
questions.explanation: David mourned for Absalom daily and desired to go to him, showing his love despite the estrangement (2 Samuel 13:37, 39).

questions.question: Which word in 2 Samuel 13:28 translated as 'valiant' in English, comes from the Hebrew meaning of being courageous and brave?
questions.correctAnswer: Chazak
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'chazak' means 'to be strong, courageous, and valiant,' used in 2 Samuel 13:28 to command the servants to be courageous.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in the account of Amnon's assassination, marked by the parallel between the murder and the subsequent flight of the king's sons?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The narrative structure of the assassination and the escape of the sons forms a chiasm emphasizing the reversal of fortune (2 Samuel 13:29-30).

questions.question: How does the theme of family betrayal in 2 Samuel 13 connect to similar themes in the New Testament?
options: It echoes Jesus’ teaching that 'a man’s foes shall be those of his own household' (Matthew 10:36)
It contradicts New Testament teachings about family unity
It is unrelated to any New Testament teaching
It is a fulfillment of the prophecy about the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes Jesus’ teaching that 'a man’s foes shall be those of his own household' (Matthew 10:36)
questions.explanation: The family strife in 2 Samuel 13 reflects Jesus’ warning in Matthew 10:36 about family divisions, showing continuity of biblical themes.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage similarly depicts the tragic consequences of family sin and betrayal, paralleling 2 Samuel 13?
options: Genesis 37, the story of Joseph and his brothers
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 37, the story of Joseph and his brothers
questions.explanation: Genesis 37 narrates sibling betrayal and conflict, paralleling the tragic family dynamics in 2 Samuel 13.

questions.question: What cultural significance did Tamar's garment of divers colours have in the context of 2 Samuel 13?
options: It identified her as a virgin daughter of the king
It was a symbol of mourning and grief
It was common attire for married women
It was a disguise to escape from Amnon
questions.correctAnswer: It identified her as a virgin daughter of the king
questions.explanation: The multicolored garment was worn by king's virgin daughters, signifying her status and purity (2 Samuel 13:18).

questions.question: How did King David respond to the news of Amnon's crime against Tamar initially, according to 2 Samuel 13?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David was very angry when he heard of Amnon’s actions (2 Samuel 13:21), but he did not take immediate action against Amnon, indicating a complex and delayed response.

questions.question: Did Absalom maintain any contact with Amnon after the assault on Tamar before the murder?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Absalom neither spoke good nor bad to Amnon because he hated him for what he did to Tamar (2 Samuel 13:22), indicating a form of continued contact but with hostility.

questions.question: What was the reason Absalom gave King David for inviting all the king’s sons to the sheepshearers’ feast?
options: To celebrate the sheepshearing and honor all brothers
To isolate Amnon and execute his plan
To discuss the king's succession plans
To seek the king’s blessing for a new army
questions.correctAnswer: To isolate Amnon and execute his plan
questions.explanation: While Absalom outwardly invited the king and his sons to the feast (2 Samuel 13:23-24), his true intent was to enact his revenge on Amnon (2 Samuel 13:28).

questions.question: What role did Jonadab, son of Shimeah, play in the events leading up to Amnon’s assault on Tamar?
options: He advised Amnon to feign illness to get Tamar to serve him
He tried to protect Tamar from Amnon
He informed King David about Amnon's intentions
He was unaware of Amnon's plans
questions.correctAnswer: He advised Amnon to feign illness to get Tamar to serve him
questions.explanation: Jonadab, described as a subtle man, advised Amnon to pretend to be sick so Tamar would come and attend him, facilitating the assault (2 Samuel 13:3-5).

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Amnon's deceit and lustful desire towards Tamar in 2 Samuel 13:1-2?
options: The doctrine of original sin and human depravity
The doctrine of justification by faith
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of original sin and human depravity
questions.explanation: Amnon's sinful desire and subsequent actions demonstrate the corruption of human nature inherited through original sin, as seen in 2 Samuel 13:1-2, showing how sin affects human will and behavior.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is indirectly challenged by the king David’s initial inaction after hearing about Amnon's sin against Tamar as described in 2 Samuel 13:21?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice
questions.explanation: David’s anger (2 Samuel 13:21) contrasts with his lack of immediate punitive action against Amnon, which can raise questions about God’s justice being enacted through human agents.

questions.question: How does Absalom’s response to Amnon’s sin in 2 Samuel 13:22-29 reveal the doctrine of retributive justice in the biblical narrative?
options: It shows human vengeance as a flawed reflection of divine justice
It illustrates God’s direct intervention to punish sin
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human vengeance as a flawed reflection of divine justice
questions.explanation: Absalom’s orchestrated killing of Amnon (2 Samuel 13:22-29) reflects human attempts at justice through vengeance, highlighting the tension between divine justice and human retribution.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 2 Samuel 13:19 and 2 Samuel 13:20 provide about the consequences of sin on the innocent?
options: Sin brings desolation and social alienation to victims
Sin only affects the guilty parties directly
Sin is always followed by immediate forgiveness
Sin has no lasting impact on family relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Sin brings desolation and social alienation to victims
questions.explanation: Tamar’s mourning (2 Samuel 13:19) and her desolation in Absalom’s house (2 Samuel 13:20) illustrate how sin’s effects extend beyond the perpetrator, causing suffering and alienation for the innocent.

questions.question: What does the narrative arc in 2 Samuel 13:37-38, where Absalom flees and stays in Geshur for three years, signify in the broader redemptive story?
options: The motif of exile and eventual restoration
The establishment of a new covenant
The immediate restoration of familial unity
questions.correctAnswer: The motif of exile and eventual restoration
questions.explanation: Absalom’s exile for three years (2 Samuel 13:37-38) fits the biblical pattern of separation due to sin, foreshadowing themes of repentance and eventual restoration central to redemptive history.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by David’s mourning for Amnon and longing for Absalom in 2 Samuel 13:39?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s compassion and patience
questions.explanation: David’s sorrow and longing (2 Samuel 13:39) reflect God’s compassionate nature, showing patience even amid human failure and brokenness.

questions.question: What combined teaching do 2 Samuel 13:5-6 and 2 Samuel 13:11 convey about the misuse of authority and deception in sin?
options: Sin often involves deceit and abuse of power to satisfy selfish desires
Sin has no impact on relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Sin often involves deceit and abuse of power to satisfy selfish desires
questions.explanation: Jonadab’s advice to feign illness and Amnon’s forceful act on Tamar (2 Samuel 13:5-6, 11) reveal how sin manipulates trust and authority for selfish ends.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 13:14-15, what does Amnon's hatred towards Tamar after the assault reveal about the nature of sin and its effects on human relationships?
options: Sin destroys true love and breeds hatred and alienation
Sin is easily overcome without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Sin destroys true love and breeds hatred and alienation
questions.explanation: Amnon’s hatred surpassing his love (2 Samuel 13:14-15) demonstrates how sin corrupts love and fractures relationships, leading to alienation.

questions.question: How does the narrative in 2 Samuel 13:28-29 illustrate the biblical principle of divine sovereignty over human actions despite human free will?
options: Absalom’s servants obey his command confidently, showing God’s sovereign orchestration
Human actions are random and uncontrolled
God abandons control during human conflict
Human free will is absolute and independent of God
questions.correctAnswer: Absalom’s servants obey his command confidently, showing God’s sovereign orchestration
questions.explanation: Though Absalom commands the killing of Amnon (2 Samuel 13:28-29), the narrative implies God’s sovereignty working through human decisions within human free will.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Samuel 13 depicts a morally flawed God who allows evil without intervention. What does 2 Samuel 13:32-33 teach about God's providential governance over human sin and justice?
options: God permits human justice to unfold but remains sovereign over outcomes
God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God permits human justice to unfold but remains sovereign over outcomes
questions.explanation: Jonadab explains the killing of Amnon was part of Absalom’s plan (2 Samuel 13:32-33), showing God’s providence permits human actions within His sovereign will, not endorsing evil but allowing human justice to proceed.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about sanctification can be drawn from Tamar’s response to Amnon’s proposal in 2 Samuel 13:12-13?
options: The call to holiness includes resisting sinful temptation
Sanctification is automatic and requires no effort
Sin is not a serious matter for the believer
questions.correctAnswer: The call to holiness includes resisting sinful temptation
questions.explanation: Tamar’s refusal and appeal to moral law (2 Samuel 13:12-13) illustrate the biblical call to holiness and active resistance to sin as part of sanctification.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 13:18's description of Tamar’s garment of divers colours symbolically relate to the biblical theme of covenant identity and purity?
options: The garment signifies royal purity and covenant identity as a virgin daughter of the king
The garment has no symbolic meaning
questions.correctAnswer: The garment signifies royal purity and covenant identity as a virgin daughter of the king
questions.explanation: The richly colored garment (2 Samuel 13:18) symbolizes Tamar’s covenant purity and royal status, underscoring the gravity of her defilement.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 2 Samuel 13:21 and 2 Samuel 13:39 provide about God’s providential use of human sorrow and repentance in redemptive history?
options: God uses human grief to lead to repentance and restoration
Sorrow has no place in redemption
questions.correctAnswer: God uses human grief to lead to repentance and restoration
questions.explanation: David’s mourning (2 Samuel 13:21, 39) shows how God works through human sorrow to bring about repentance and eventual healing in the redemptive narrative.

questions.question: What narrative role does Jonadab play in 2 Samuel 13, and what does this teach about human complicity in sin according to the chapter?
options: Jonadab’s cunning advice enables sin, showing human complicity in facilitating evil
Jonadab is a symbol of divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: Jonadab’s cunning advice enables sin, showing human complicity in facilitating evil
questions.explanation: Jonadab’s counsel to Amnon (2 Samuel 13:3-6) reveals how human complicity and subtlety can contribute to sinful acts, emphasizing responsibility for enabling sin.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 13:30-31, how does David’s reaction to the news of the deaths initially reported reflect biblical teaching on grief and human limitation?
options: David’s tearing of garments and lying on the earth express profound grief and human vulnerability in suffering
questions.correctAnswer: David’s tearing of garments and lying on the earth express profound grief and human vulnerability in suffering
questions.explanation: David’s response (2 Samuel 13:30-31) typifies biblical mourning practices, reflecting the depth of human pain and limitation in the face of tragedy.
